active_goal.objective: Ship a production-ready Sfora learned-vector-space retrieval library whose deployed image-to-top-k system surpasses the strongest protocol-matched published quality reference on BOTH SOP and DeepFashion In-Shop and is faster end-to-end at matched quality, hardware, cache, batch size and gallery scale. Keep useful Rust/CUDA/CuTile code, exact packed top-k/tie semantics, clean packages, bounded resources and reproducible tests; no paper-only result. Preserve all current Sfora work, consultations and DGX jobs, inspect before launching, and do not duplicate. Current verified exploratory anchors: three-seed public-config SOP official TEST packed R@1 91.7419% versus dated UNICOM 91.2%, but TEST was previously observed and no matched full-pipeline speed win exists; older three-seed In-Shop official query/gallery packed R@1 95.4823% versus UNICOM 96.7%, while the newer true-freeze checkpoint has no official result. Its TRAIN holdout diagnostic got 97.6235% on 6,354 queries, but this is not an official or scale-projected result; impostor-count misses are sublinear, so the linear scaling premise failed. The selected SOP batch-1 p99 diagnostic was 19.622 versus 19.606 ms, not a speed win; batch-32 global thread reduction failed p99. CUB transfer gain is positive, Cars transfer inconclusive. Treat all these as evidence, not SOTA claims. Diagnose the concrete In-Shop quality gap and the public image-to-result latency bottleneck from existing receipts; pick ONE cheapest causally distinct TRAIN-only intervention, with a predeclared stop rule, instead of another series of unbounded probes or loss tweaks. Consider representation, architecture, data coverage, sampling, supervision, training algorithm, compression, preprocessing and serving; use psychology/physics/other-field inspiration only when it yields a testable mechanism. Freeze method and checkpoint selection on TRAIN identities; compare matched backbone, data, compute budget, scorer and paired seeds, report R@1/mAP@R and class/query uncertainty. Qualify both official protocols, plus CUB and Cars transfer, distinguishing exploratory official reads from new independent confirmation. Preserve actual packed-score quality; exact output parity is mandatory for kernel changes. Measure training time, images/s and VRAM and full decode/preprocess/encoder/packing/native-search/image-to-top-k p50/p95/p99 and QPS at batch1 and batch32, same hardware and query/gallery. A p99 product claim needs 10,000 interleaved paired calls and a confidence interval. Run GPU work only on authenticated DGX Spark after cheaper local/CPU falsifiers, with raw receipts and cost. Use Opus 5.5 plus GPT-6 Astra for consequential critique and Fable for truly new research, without duplicate jobs. If either quality or speed fails, change the responsible layer and stop negative arms early. Within 24 hours push a substantive library/training increment and concise verified decision table with datasets, splits, controls, quality, speed, uncertainty and next gate; continue until the production joint quality-and-speed target is met.

reviewers.partial_result:
**GO-with-concrete-corrections, for one bounded TRAIN-only utility experiment.** The paired design isolates a scientifically distinct supervision effect. Existing evidence does **not** establish that it will produce a useful production model or close the joint quality-and-speed gap.

The old verdict remains **KILL**: seed069 loses one recall query, so the per-seed gate fails before bootstrap or validation admission. Mean gains and useful Pareto endpoints remain valid development evidence. The fixed triples’ unchanged violations establish no demonstrated mechanism on that panel; they do not establish an architecture ceiling. [Terminal verification](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/evidence/compact_metric/sop-siglip2-substrate-v1/fullfeature-residual-full-selection-score-v1/verification.json), [existing churn evidence](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/evidence/compact_metric/sop-siglip2-substrate-v1/fullfeature-residual-full-selection-score-v1/existing-receipt-churn.json).

The rationale is defensible: R@1 depends on the best eligible positive beating the best wrong identity, whereas the current SmoothAP objective averages contributions across all positives. The proposed hinge explicitly supervises that boundary. Detached **index selection**, followed by gathering from the original connected scores, gives the appropriate selected-max gradient away from ties; deterministic original-row tie resolution makes the boundary reproducible. This is an extension of the existing nearest-ranking objective, with live gallery gradients and matched full-feature capacity.

The closest measured predecessor is the retired **A-only compact hinge**, which improved R1 but reduced AP. The earlier four-tensor encoder trainer supplies the selection oracle and is a different experiment. Keeping SmoothAP unchanged does not guarantee AP preservation: the auxiliary gradient changes the direction entering global clipping and AdamW. Its `.05` normalization also makes coefficient1 a substantive intervention. [Recorded predecessor results](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_smooth_ap_plan_2026-10-04.md:35).

The smallest corrections are:

1. **Authenticate the correct control correspondence.** The new control must reproduce the archived **full-feature candidate objective**, including both `A` and `C` gradients. The current historical objective authenticator points to the earlier current-gallery source; its A-only correspondence cannot establish the new control’s complete gradient behavior. Pin the terminal full-feature closure and use the already prescribed first-B64 witnesses. Initial forward equality at `C=0` alone is insufficient. [Authenticator](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:852).

2. **Extend the schema change through every admission boundary.** Current parameter roles, forward dispatch, payload checks, portable loading, evaluator oracle and confirmation freezer encode frozen-zero control `C`. Both new arms must admit trainable `[A,C]`, restored moments, and updated nonzero `C`; both serving arms must execute the residual. Version or replace the method-specific launcher adapters as well as trainer/evaluator closures. Preserve the archived validators and receipts. The completed plan’s four-file implementation boundary is therefore incomplete. [Trainer roles](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:427), [evaluator oracle](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/evaluate_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1304), [confirmation assumptions](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/freeze_fullfeature_confirmation_cpu.py:270).

3. **Clarify singleton and reduction semantics.** Singleton **anchors** have regression only. Singleton gallery rows remain eligible wrong-identity negatives and can receive gallery-side ranking gradients. Suppressing those gradients would change the proposed objective. `K` counts valid anchor occurrences in the full scheduled B64; `.05·2K` remains shared across both views and all micros. At `K=0`, return a connected zero without positive indexing. Reuse the deterministic selector, not the old frozen-teacher `mine/loss_terms`. [Current membership and loss](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:809), [old miner](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_nearest_ranking.py:637).

4. **Make the production bridge concrete before launch.** Portable image-to-packed inference exists, but the shipped public encoder currently requires a 1024-dimensional linear head; this experiment uses 1152-dimensional features and `A/C`. Name the integration boundary, full-production InShop/SOP training transition, checkpoint-selection rule, and protocol-matched published comparators. The current trainer is hard-coded to TRAIN6355/1008 and cannot simply become the full SOP runner. These are release-plan corrections, not additional research experiments. [Portable inference](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1440), [public encoder geometry](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/src/sfora/siglip2_compact_serving.py:127).

Execution appears feasible within the frozen time caps, but memory ownership matters: previous CPU qualification peaked only about **90 MiB below 8 GiB**. Release witness graphs and parameter copies before constructing inference models. Charge actual selection, transfers and auxiliary backward to candidate core; do not inflate control with dummy work. Historical cost ratios cannot qualify this new pair. [Resource evidence](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_fullfeature_residual_plan_2026-10-04.md:11).

Keep every frozen quality/resource/integrity gate unchanged. Reused selection and its conditional bootstrap remain adaptive development evidence, not independent confirmation. Only the new full GO admits the sealed validation panel.

The hinge disappears at inference; the residual computation and encoder remain. Consequently, this experiment supplies **no intrinsic speed mechanism**. A survivor must proceed directly through confirmation, both official protocol-matched quality gates, and actual public B1/B32 image-to-top-k measurements with the required 10,000 paired calls and p99 interval. Another failed gate closes this recipe without extra updates or tuning.

I verified that the current trainer/evaluator hashes match the terminal receipt. No files were edited or experiments launched.

**GO-with-concrete-corrections for one bounded TRAIN experiment. No production release approval.** The mechanism is scientifically distinct and testable; existing evidence does **not** establish that it will likely reach the joint quality-and-speed target.

The old hinge uses frozen teacher scores ([nearest trainer:637](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_nearest_ranking.py:637)). The proposal adds first-hit supervision to the current connected gallery while retaining all-positive SmoothAP. Identical trainable `[A,C]` arms isolate that intervention. This justifies the fixed experiment, without rescuing the previous KILL or attributing its one-query regression to a demonstrated cause.

The concrete corrections and blockers are:

1. **P1 — Migrate the complete objective and state contract, including receipt arithmetic.** Current control still freezes and excludes C from AdamW ([trainer:548](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:548)); the evaluator explicitly expects that allocation ([evaluator:949](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/evaluate_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:949)). More subtly, receipts require equal initial arm gradients, `rank ≤ 1`, and `loss = mse + rank` ([gradient checks:1969](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1969), [step checks:1724](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1724)). Keep SmoothAP and auxiliary hinge values/activity separate; authenticate the candidate’s additional term and both arms’ C updates, moments, resume state and nonzero-C serving witnesses. New schemas must reject old receipts without weakening their historical checks.

2. **P1 — Prove the hinge’s gallery gradient independently of SmoothAP.** Existing witnesses detach the whole ranking gallery and compare against an older A-only objective ([CPU witness:1018](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:1018)). SmoothAP’s valid gallery gradient could conceal a mistakenly detached hinge. Within the planned single qualification, require **hinge-only** query/gallery decomposition for both A and C, and reject a mutant detaching **only the hinge gallery**. Pin the archived full-feature candidate as the new control’s objective oracle; initial forward equality alone cannot establish C-gradient correspondence. Preserve the existing nonzero-C oracle and full64/micro16 checks.

3. **P2 — Clarify singleton semantics and preserve exact selection.** “Singletons receive regression only” in the completed plan must mean **singleton anchors**. Singleton gallery rows remain eligible wrong-identity negatives and can receive ranking gradients. The current membership logic includes them ([membership:809](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py:809)). Do not remove or detach those rows. The proposed `H/(.05·2K)` denominator is correct across both views and all micros. Filter invalid anchors before indexing; select by original-row ties from detached scores, then gather from that same connected tensor. Include unsorted original-row ties, mixed-valid micros and all-invalid anchors in the existing falsifier.

4. **P1 for release — The actual public image-to-top-k adapter remains missing.** The packaged encoder requires a **1024→128 linear head** and rejects other geometry ([constructor:123](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/src/sfora/siglip2_compact_serving.py:123), [packing:261](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/src/sfora/siglip2_compact_serving.py:261)). This experiment uses 1152-feature concat-plus-C inference. Its portable loader produces descriptors/wires, but that does not qualify the packaged public index. Make the serving milestone explicit: load the surviving complete checkpoint, reproduce packed outputs and native IDs/ties, and exercise user gallery construction plus public B1/B32 queries. Preserve image limits, dependency isolation and checkpoint authentication. The absent training term establishes no latency win.

5. **P2 — Resource feasibility has narrow margins.** Previous CPU qualification peaked at **8,495,210,496 bytes**, only **90 MiB below 8 GiB** ([verification](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/evidence/compact_metric/sop-siglip2-substrate-v1/fullfeature-residual-cpu-v1/verification.json:7)). Release historical/oracle graphs and temporary score copies sequentially before inference construction. Previous full scoring took **454.156/500 seconds**, but skipped bootstrap; it does not prove the successful bootstrap path fits ([terminal verification](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/evidence/compact_metric/sop-siglip2-substrate-v1/fullfeature-residual-full-selection-score-v1/verification.json:26)). Keep every whole-unit cap and fresh whole/core ratio unchanged; charge candidate mining/transfers/backward, without padding control work.

The scientific risk remains real: earlier hinge supervision improved R1 while reducing AP ([history:35](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_smooth_ap_plan_2026-10-04.md:35)). Retaining SmoothAP does not guarantee its benefit survives the added gradients and shared clipping. The unchanged per-seed AP/R1 gates therefore remain decisive.

Selection has already informed several interventions. Its paired intervals describe conditional development evidence, not independent confirmation or broad seed uncertainty. Preserve the same-four sealed validation gate, then freeze full production training, checkpoint selection and protocol-matched SOP/InShop comparisons. Both official quality results and the matched public 10,000-pair p99 interval remain mandatory.

I verified that current trainer/evaluator/test hashes match the terminal source pins and that the receipt hash matches its verification. **Original KILL, zero bootstrap draws, no VAL admission and retained Pareto endpoints remain intact.** No files were edited, tests run, or jobs launched.
